builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Ambessa: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (4,180 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 54.6% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile physical fighter who weaves empowered attacks between ability dashes to sustain energy and stay on a target. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Eclipse → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance. Grasp of the Undying keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Maw of Malmortius, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Eclipse → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance, with Grasp of the Undying.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Eclipse → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 54.6% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Eclipse → Spear of Shojin → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
When Ambessa is casting an Ability, issuing a Move or Attack order will cause her to dash in that direction after the Ability finishes.

Each cast initiation grants her a charge for [4] seconds (max: [3]). While Ambessa has a charge, she gains [75] %i:scaleRange% Attack Range and [0.5] %i:scaleAS% Attack Speed. Attacks consume a charge to deal [characterLevelInterpolation(5 → 25; raw flags preserved) + (0.2) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and restore [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=40, perLevel=0, changes=[{"mLevel": 7, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 13, "mAdditionalBonusAtThisLevel": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])] Energy.

Cunning Sweep: Ambessa sweeps her blades forward, dealing [40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 + (0.6) × AD[statFormula=2]] + [0.04 / 0.045 / 0.05 / 0.055 / 0.06 + (0.0003) × AD[statFormula=2]] max Health physical damage to enemies at the edge of the strike. All other enemies take [0.5] damage. Striking an enemy readies a Sundering Slam.

Sundering Slam: Ambessa slams her blades down, dealing [50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 + (0.9) × AD[statFormula=2]] + [0.04 / 0.045 / 0.05 / 0.055 / 0.06 + (0.0004) × AD[statFormula=2]] max Health physical damage against the first enemy hit. All other enemies take [0.5] damage.

Passive: Ambessa gains [(0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3) × 100]% %i:scaleAPen% Armor Penetration and her Abilities heal her for [0.15 / 0.175 / 0.2 + (0.5) × Stat(18)] of the damage she dealt.

Active: Ambessa becomes Unstoppable and blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, Suppressing the target for [0.75] seconds and then slamming them into the ground, dealing [150 / 250 / 350 + (0.8) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and Stunning them for [0.4] seconds.

Ambessa gains [characterLevelInterpolation(50 → 320; raw flags preserved) + (1.5) × AD[statFormula=2]] Shield for [1.5] seconds and braces herself for [0.5] seconds. She then slams the ground, dealing [50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 + (0.5) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage to nearby enemies, which increases to [(50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 + (0.5) × AD[statFormula=2]) × (1.5)] physical damage if she braced herself from damage from an enemy champion, large monster, or structure.

Ambessa whips her chains around, dealing [40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 + (0.5) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and Slowing enemies by [99]%, which decays over [1] second. Initiating {{Spell_AmbessaP_Name}} from this Ability will trigger an additional strike.

builds.name: Energy Charge Strikes
builds.summary: Count casts possible from a fixed starting Energy pool.
builds.goal: Count casts possible from a fixed starting Energy pool.
builds.hypothesis: P attack charges grant range/speed and restore Energy when consumed. Trinity and Sundered Sky reward cast-attack weaving; Shojin improves basic availability while Death's Dance buys time for R ability healing.
testPlan: Required state: Issue a move/attack command during each cast and consume four-second charges.
Count casts possible from a fixed starting Energy pool; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Kiting denies energy refunds despite haste.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Haste alone does not fund additional casts.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Trinity Force, Sundered Sky, Spear of Shojin, Death's Dance, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Ambessa: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile physical fighter who weaves empowered attacks between ability dashes to sustain energy and stay on a target. Do empowered attacks between dashes sustain energy and contact? More attacks do not help if spell timing or dash access fails; measure Q edges and energy starvation. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Ambessa: Do empowered attacks between dashes sustain energy and contact? More attacks do not help if spell timing or dash access fails; measure Q edges and energy starvation.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Energy. Do not treat mana regeneration as Energy recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Ambessa sweeps her twin drakehounds in a semicircle in front of her, dealing bonus damage to enemies hit by the blades. Striking an enemy will transform the next cast of this ability for a short period of time, causing her to slam her twin drakehounds down in a line in front of her, dealing bonus damage to the first enemy hit. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Ambessa's stated kit question: Do empowered attacks between dashes sustain energy and contact? More attacks do not help if spell timing or dash access fails; measure Q edges and energy starvation.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Energy. Do not treat mana regeneration as Energy recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Brace Chain Retention
builds.summary: Compare braced W and dash-enabled E against missed brace/no dash.
builds.goal: Compare braced W and dash-enabled E against missed brace/no dash.
builds.hypothesis: W gains retaliation damage only after bracing a qualifying hit; E gains another strike when initiating P. Eclipse rewards separate hits and Cleaver supports physical packets; Stridebreaker retains proximity after E's brief slow.
testPlan: Required state: Brace incoming champion damage then dash with E.
Compare braced W and dash-enabled E against missed brace/no dash; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Unbraced W or an outward dash loses damage.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Multiple packets do not prove instant full Cleaver stacks.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Eclipse, Black Cleaver, Stridebreaker, Sterak's Gage, Death's Dance, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
